trust_decision.summary: Bytes of a chunk read from the file (minbits, minval size, packed payload) are trusted as fitting inside the chunk buffer when the scale-offset filter decodes it, in H5Z__filter_scaleoffset (reverse path) and H5Z__scaleoffset_decompress_one_byte.

landing_point.why: Reverse (decompress) branch of the scale-offset filter callback; the summary names the scale-offset filter and a crafted chunk.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: unknown: the recorded fix commit changes no source code, so there is no published scope to argue from.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: unknown (candidate: the full-precision case, minbits == p.size*8, must still copy the stored raw chunk unchanged; not tied to a published fix)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Full-precision branch copies size_out bytes from *buf + 21 without comparing against *buf_size, unlike the header checks at 1208 and 1226.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same filter's decode path; the existing header checks only cover 5 + minval_size bytes, so a maintainer hardening the bit unpacker could plausibly skip the memcpy branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: *buf_size - buf_offset is passed as the payload length while only 5 + minval_size bytes are proven present (1226), so a chunk shorter than 21 bytes is not ruled out before the subtraction.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Header length check and payload offset use different constants (5 + minval_size vs buf_offset = 21 at src/H5Zscaleoffset.c:1115).
